fields.title: Why "looks fine" does not work
fields.keyTakeaway: Evals check answer properties rather than exact matches against a reference, run on every change, and separate search quality from generation quality.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: We changed the prompt. Did it get better or worse?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Without measurement, an AI feature improves blindly: every prompt change can fix one thing and break another, and no one will notice. Products that live without evals discover degradation months later through complaints.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: **[[evaluation|Evals]]** are systematic testing on a fixed set of examples.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: Evals check answer properties rather than exact matches against a reference, run on every change, and separate search quality from generation quality.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **[[eval-set|Eval set]].** 100–300 examples covering typical requests, edge cases, and known problems. Assembled from real requests rather than invented.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Criteria.** What we check. Not match against a reference — answers are variable — but properties:
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: *Factual precision.* Does the answer contain a correct fact, are there incorrect ones. *[[grounding|Grounding]].* Is the answer based on data from the context. *Format.* Are structure, length, and mandatory parts observed. *Safety.* Is there an answer where a refusal should be. *Search recall.* Did the required document make it into the context. A separate metric separating RAG from generation.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **Evaluation method.** Three options, usually used together:
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: *Programmatic check.* Format, presence of mandatory fields, length. Cheap and reliable. *[[llm-as-judge|LLM-as-a-judge]].* A model evaluates the answer against criteria. Cheap, scalable, requires validating the judge itself. *Human.* Expensive, applied to a subsample and disputed cases.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Key rule: **evals are run on every prompt, model, or data change.** Otherwise, they turn into a one-off exercise.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: A set of 240 questions: 120 typical, 60 edge cases (negations, rare products, missing data), 40 forbidden (medical, non-product), 20 from "inaccurate" feedback.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: A run takes 12 minutes and costs about 40 rubles. It runs automatically upon prompt changes.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Over half a year, evals caught four regressions. The most telling: editing the instruction for answer brevity reduced the share of answers with a source citation from 100% to 71%. No one would have noticed for months.
fields.sections/3/blocks/5/text: The threshold for refusals is 100%, and this is the only hard one: any drop blocks the change.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: The eval set ages: the product changes, new types of requests appear. It should be replenished quarterly from real logs and feedback.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Evals check answer properties rather than exact matches against a reference, run on every change, and separate search quality from generation quality.
